status: Proposed research-to-feature plan; production implementation has not been started or approved by this report.
objective: Improve prediction of executable morning-entry to same-day-close returns after a selloff, rather than identify an exact future bottom.
user_clarification: The aim is feature iteration alongside the existing feature set. Standalone cohort averages do not establish whether a feature adds predictive information to Rank or Fit. Precise candidate flags and their underlying continuous measurements are defined in trigger_candidates.json.

priority_features.name: Long-term low location and fresh break
priority_features.question: Is the entry near a previously observed floor, or below it?
priority_features.formula: low252 = min(L[t-252:t]); distance = O[t] / low252 - 1; breach = O[t] < low252; low_age = sessions since the most recent occurrence of low252.
priority_features.timing: Prior low and its age are pre-open; distance and breach require the observed opening price.
priority_features.novelty: The current pipeline has short-range patterns and trailing-peak drawdowns, but no genuine 252-session low context.
priority_features.guard: Do not use today's eventual low. Require 252 completed valid sessions and distinguish missing history from a neutral value.

priority_features.name: Selloff severity and recovery already consumed
priority_features.question: How unusually large was the decline, and how much has recovered before entry?
priority_features.formula: two_day_return = C[t-1] / C[t-3] - 1; severity = two_day_return / (std20(returns ending t-3) * sqrt(2)); close_loss_recovered = (O[t] - C[t-1]) / (C[t-3] - C[t-1]), defined only for a positive prior closing loss.
priority_features.timing: Severity is pre-open; recovery fraction requires the observed open.
priority_features.novelty: The two-day return already exists. The proposed addition is recovery fraction and its interaction with long-term low context, using volatility measured before the shock.
priority_features.guard: Negative fractions mean continued decline; values above one mean more than the closing loss recovered. Do not clip these cases together. A separate low-based recovery fraction uses a different denominator and must have a different name.

priority_features.name: Selling-pressure change during the decline
priority_features.question: Was the second down day less forceful, and did buyers lift the price away from its low?
priority_features.formula: Compare absolute prior daily losses, true ranges and dollar volumes between t-2 and t-1, scaled by baselines ending t-3; retain yesterday's close location (C-L)/(H-L) and lower-wick fraction as interaction inputs.
priority_features.timing: All inputs stop at yesterday's close.
priority_features.novelty: Volume, candle shapes and volatility already exist. Test incremental interactions conditional on selloff/low location rather than add duplicate indicators.
priority_features.guard: High volume can reflect new information as well as temporary selling. No current-day full-session volume. Zero-range bars and missing denominators need explicit handling.

priority_features.name: Current gap and previous selling volume
priority_features.question: Does the market open stronger after heavy selling, or continue to break down?
priority_features.formula: gap[t] = O[t] / C[t-1] - 1; gap_previous_volume = gap[t] * volume_zscore[t-1], optionally interacted with prior selloff severity.
priority_features.timing: Open-known; must be calculated identically in historical rows and live inference.
priority_features.novelty: Existing gap_volume_interaction uses same-day completed volume and is shifted as a whole. It therefore represents yesterday's gap times yesterday's volume, not this interaction.
priority_features.guard: An opening gap does not establish that a bottom has formed. Observing the open does not guarantee an execution at that exact price.

secondary_hypotheses: Separate the prior two-day loss into overnight and regular-session components. The timing literature gives a strong reason to avoid treating them as interchangeable; overlap with existing session-pattern features needs ablation.
Distinguish a market-wide decline from stock-specific residual selling, using lagged SPY exposure and, if point-in-time data become available, sector and timestamped news context.
A 09:35 or 09:45 stabilization/reclaim feature is a separate delayed-entry experiment. Use only completed bars, enter after the signal, and retain same-day close as the exit.

phases.name: Freeze compatible historical inputs
phases.work: Resolve production one-year history versus the required 252-session warmup. Preserve a frozen provider/basis/universe snapshot; obtain at least 504 completed sessions, preferably a five-year research panel, before feature evaluation. Certify actions and raw/adjusted price compatibility, symbol mapping, and missing bars. Keep this separate from live stores.
phases.verification: Check split/ex-dividend/spinoff examples, history warmup, provider symbol mappings, as-of universe coverage, and reproducible hashes.
phases.guards: Do not silently substitute 251 sessions for a 252-session low, assume five-year corporate-action certification, or call current-universe data point-in-time.

phases.name: Build small, continuous candidate families in isolation
phases.work: Implement one pure dip-context feature module, using the existing pipeline and metadata registration patterns. Keep continuous measurements plus the precise candidate flags in trigger_candidates.json; reuse existing components instead of duplicating them. Classify every column as pre-open/close-known or open-known, and mirror open-known recomputation in live rows. Keep candidate artifacts separate until the incremental experiment is assessed.
phases.verification: Use hand-calculated examples, missing-history and zero-denominator cases; perturb current/future HLCV and prove morning inputs unchanged; assert historical and live rows match. Run metadata completeness and focused feature/dataset tests, then required build checks.
phases.guards: No current high/low/close/full-day volume in a morning input; no accidental double shifting; no new per-ticker return-mean buckets without sample-count and shrinkage treatment.

phases.name: Measure incremental value against current Rank and Fit
phases.work: Compare baseline, each candidate family, and a predeclared small combined set on identical chronological folds and eligible rows. Track Rank IC, top-20 and top-5 gross/net returns, turnover, downside, and coverage by era/regime. Test thresholds and choices within training dates only. Keep the fixed production ticker exclusion out of feature search; an already-consulted ticker sample is not pristine validation.
phases.verification: Paired date/weekly uncertainty; several strictly later date blocks; full results including failures; realistic cost sensitivity and a registered forward paper period. Confirm improvement is incremental to existing returns/volume/candle features.
phases.guards: No shuffled k-fold, no tuning on held-out ticker outcomes, no promoting a family based only on MRCY, a positive pooled average, or one favorable fold. Do not turn raw Rank scores into probabilities.

phases.name: Validate executable morning entry and then decide on production
phases.work: For open-conditioned rules, freeze a new representative minute-bar sample and test the first executable entry after the decision, including delayed individual stock openings. Compare 09:35/09:45 candidates only in their own entry-to-close experiments. After validation, present the concrete feature/model changes and results for a production decision.
phases.verification: Decision precedes execution; early closes, DST, halts, delayed opens, missing bars, spreads/slippage, and sell-before-close timing are explicit. Report participation and all rejected observations.
phases.guards: Do not use the hindsight daily minimum as the purchase price or carry a failed same-day setup overnight to improve the label.
